title: Java for enterprise development
answer: Java is widely used for enterprise systems because the JVM is mature and portable, the language is statically typed, and the ecosystem provides strong tooling, testing, build automation, security, persistence, observability, concurrency, and web frameworks. Spring Boot and Maven make it practical to assemble large applications from well-supported components, while the JVM provides garbage collection, JIT compilation, diagnostics, and long-term runtime stability. The trade-offs are real: Java applications can use more memory than smaller runtimes, cold startup can be slower, framework stacks can become complex, dependency and build configuration require discipline, and teams must manage JVM, library, and framework upgrades. Modern Java reduces some historical verbosity, and newer runtime techniques can improve startup and footprint, but enterprise Java still rewards structured engineering over minimal setup. AeroTopo will use these strengths where they fit, while later lessons will expose the operational and architectural costs instead of hiding them.

steps.title: Open the AeroTopo project in IntelliJ
steps.why: Start by grounding the discussion in the project we will build. IntelliJ is the only IDE used in this course. The project is configured for Java 21 so later lessons can connect language features, tooling, testing, Spring, persistence, security, and operations to one cumulative codebase.
steps.question: Enterprise Java projects can span many packages, frameworks, build files, and runtime settings, so understanding the workspace before editing reduces blind changes. Why should you first open the complete AeroTopo project in IntelliJ before evaluating Java for enterprise development?
steps.why_te: Manam build cheyyaboye real AeroTopo project nundi discussion start chestunnam. Ee course lo IDE ga IntelliJ matrame use chestam. Java 21 configuration later lessons lo language features, tooling, testing, Spring, persistence, security mariyu operations ni oka cumulative codebase tho connect cheyyadaniki base istundi.

steps.title: Inspect the Maven project descriptor
steps.why: The enterprise advantage is not just the Java syntax. A major strength is the surrounding ecosystem. Maven gives the project a reproducible dependency and build model, while Spring Boot supplies a mature application framework on top of the JVM.
steps.question: In the cumulative AeroTopo learning project, the "Inspect the Maven project descriptor" step connects this concept to a visible IntelliJ workflow and keeps enough technical context for later lessons instead of reducing it to a short interview phrase. Maven gives Java teams a reproducible project model for dependencies, plugins, compilation, testing, and packaging. How does inspecting AeroTopo's `pom.xml` help you understand one of Java's major enterprise strengths and one of its complexity costs?
steps.why_te: Enterprise advantage Java syntax matrame kaadu; surrounding ecosystem kuda mukhyam. Maven reproducible dependency mariyu build model istundi, Spring Boot JVM paina mature application framework ni andistundi.

steps.title: Focus on the Spring Boot parent
steps.why: The Spring Boot parent centralizes compatible dependency and plugin defaults. This is an enterprise advantage because teams can standardize builds and reduce version mismatch, but it also illustrates a trade-off: framework conventions and dependency graphs add layers that developers must understand and maintain.
steps.question: In the cumulative AeroTopo learning project, the "Focus on the Spring Boot parent" step connects this concept to a visible IntelliJ workflow and keeps enough technical context for later lessons instead of reducing it to a short interview phrase. Spring Boot's parent POM supplies coordinated dependency and plugin defaults so teams do not manually align every version. Why is this centralized version management useful in enterprise Java, and what dependency-management trade-off does it introduce?
steps.why_te: Spring Boot parent compatible dependency mariyu plugin defaults ni centralize chestundi. Dini valla teams versions ni standardize cheyyagalavu; ade samayam lo framework conventions mariyu dependency graph ni ardham chesukovali.

steps.title: Inspect the starter dependencies
steps.why: The web, validation, and test starters demonstrate Java's broad enterprise ecosystem. Instead of implementing HTTP handling, validation, and test infrastructure from scratch, the project composes proven libraries. The cost is a larger dependency surface and more framework knowledge than a tiny standalone program requires.
steps.question: Enterprise Java applications usually assemble capabilities such as web handling, validation, persistence, security, and testing from libraries instead of rebuilding them. What advantage does AeroTopo gain from Spring Boot starter dependencies, and what maintenance cost comes with a larger dependency graph?
steps.why_te: Web, validation mariyu test starters enterprise ecosystem breadth ni chupistayi. HTTP handling, validation, testing infrastructure ni scratch nundi build cheyyakunda proven libraries ni compose chestam; kani dependency surface mariyu framework knowledge perugutayi.

steps.title: Open IntelliJ External Libraries
steps.why: IntelliJ can resolve the JDK and Maven libraries directly into the project model. Strong IDE support is one of Java's practical advantages in large codebases: navigation, refactoring, debugging, inspections, dependency awareness, and test integration all work against the same typed project model.
steps.question: In the cumulative AeroTopo learning project, the "Open IntelliJ External Libraries" step connects this concept to a visible IntelliJ workflow and keeps enough technical context for later lessons instead of reducing it to a short interview phrase. A statically typed Java project lets IntelliJ index the JDK and resolved Maven libraries for navigation, refactoring, inspections, and debugging. Why does strong IDE awareness become especially valuable as an enterprise codebase grows?
steps.why_te: IntelliJ JDK mariyu Maven libraries ni direct ga project model lo resolve chestundi. Large codebase lo navigation, refactoring, debugging, inspections, dependency awareness mariyu tests same typed model meeda work cheyyadam strong advantage.

steps.title: Inspect the Java application entry point
steps.why: The application starts from a normal Java main method and then hands control to Spring Boot. Java's explicit types and predictable entry points help large teams navigate and refactor systems safely, while Spring adds substantial runtime behavior that developers must learn rather than treating as magic.
steps.question: In the cumulative AeroTopo learning project, the "Inspect the Java application entry point" step connects this concept to a visible IntelliJ workflow and keeps enough technical context for later lessons instead of reducing it to a short interview phrase. A Java application still begins from an explicit entry point even when a framework controls most runtime behavior. What does AeroTopo's `main` method reveal about the boundary between ordinary Java execution and Spring Boot framework startup?
steps.why_te: Application normal Java `main` method nundi start ayi tarvata Spring Boot ki control istundi. Explicit Java entry point clear ga untundi; Spring runtime behavior additional abstraction ga vastundi.

steps.title: Focus on the Spring Boot application declaration
steps.why: A single annotation activates a large amount of framework behavior through auto-configuration and component scanning. That productivity is valuable in enterprise work, but the abstraction can make startup behavior and configuration harder to understand unless the team learns what the framework is doing.
steps.question: In the cumulative AeroTopo learning project, the "Focus on the Spring Boot application declaration" step connects this concept to a visible IntelliJ workflow and keeps enough technical context for later lessons instead of reducing it to a short interview phrase. `@SpringBootApplication` enables component scanning and auto-configuration with a small amount of source code. Why does this improve enterprise productivity while also requiring developers to understand framework behavior that is not visible directly in the class?
steps.why_te: Oka annotation tho auto-configuration mariyu component scanning activate avutayi. Productivity ekkuva avutundi, kani framework em chestundo ardham kakapothe startup behavior mariyu configuration confusing ga anipinchachu.

steps.title: Open IntelliJ's integrated terminal
steps.why: Enterprise Java development is not limited to the editor. The same IntelliJ workspace can expose the terminal for JDK, Maven, Git, test, and diagnostic commands. We keep those development commands inside IntelliJ for this learning project rather than switching to another IDE.
steps.question: In the cumulative AeroTopo learning project, the "Open IntelliJ's integrated terminal" step connects this concept to a visible IntelliJ workflow and keeps enough technical context for later lessons instead of reducing it to a short interview phrase. Enterprise Java work includes build, Git, JVM, test, and diagnostic commands in addition to editing source files. Why is using IntelliJ's integrated terminal useful for keeping those workflows inside the same project context?
steps.why_te: Enterprise development editor tho matrame ayipodu. IntelliJ integrated terminal lo JDK, Maven, Git, test mariyu diagnostic commands run cheyyadam valla context switch taggipoyi same project lo workflow untundi.

steps.title: Confirm the Java runtime from IntelliJ
steps.why: The JVM is both a strength and an operational responsibility. A managed runtime provides garbage collection, JIT compilation, diagnostics, threading, and portability, but production teams still need to understand runtime versions, memory behavior, startup characteristics, and tuning. Later lessons will make those costs visible instead of presenting Java as universally better.
steps.question: The JVM provides portability, garbage collection, JIT compilation, diagnostics, and a managed runtime, but teams must still control runtime versions and operational behavior. After confirming Java 21 with `java --version`, how would you summarize the main advantages and disadvantages of Java for enterprise development?
steps.why_te: Managed JVM GC, JIT, diagnostics, threading mariyu portability istundi. Production team runtime versions, memory behavior, startup mariyu tuning ni kuda ardham chesukovali; kabatti benefits tho paatu operational costs kuda evaluate cheyyali.
